name: Ujjayanta Palace
description: Former royal palace of the Manikya dynasty in central Agartala, now the Tripura State Museum. Built 1899-1901 by Maharaja Radha Kishore Manikya in Indo-Saracenic style with three domes; set amid Mughal gardens and two artificial lakes.
facts: Built 1899-1901 by Maharaja Radha Kishore Manikya
Named by Rabindranath Tagore
Housed State Legislative Assembly until 2011
Now houses Tripura State Museum showcasing Northeast cultures

name: Pushpabanta Palace (Kunjaban Palace)
description: Former royal retreat and Raj Bhavan on a hillock in northern Agartala, built in 1917 by Maharaja Birendra Kishore Manikya. Served as Governor's residence until 2018; associated with Rabindranath Tagore's visits.
facts: Built 1917 by Maharaja Birendra Kishore Manikya
Former official Raj Bhavan until 2018
Rabindranath Tagore stayed here in 1926
Located about 1 km north of Ujjayanta Palace

name: Jagannath Temple
description: 19th-century Hindu temple within the Ujjayanta Palace grounds dedicated to Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra. Features octagonal base and distinctive orange stepped shikharas in Tripura style.
facts: Located inside Ujjayanta Palace complex
Built by Maharaja Radha Kishore Manikya
Octagonal base with four-storey orange shikharas
Famous for evening aarti and annual Rath Yatra

name: Chaturdasha Devata Temple
description: Historic temple in Old Agartala dedicated to the fourteen deities (Chaturdasha Devata), built in 1761 by King Krishna Manikya. Features Tripuri dome architecture; main venue for the annual Kharchi Puja festival.
facts: Built 1761 by King Krishna Manikya
Dedicated to 14 tribal and Hindu deities
Venue of major Kharchi Puja festival each July
About 8 km from central Agartala

name: Lakshmi Narayan Temple
description: Vaishnavite temple within the Ujjayanta Palace grounds dedicated to Lakshmi Narayana, constructed during the reign of Maharaja Birendra Kishore Manikya (1909-1923).
facts: Located in Ujjayanta Palace compound
Built during 1909-1923 by Birendra Kishore Manikya
Dedicated to the divine couple Lakshmi and Narayana
Part of the royal temple cluster

name: Heritage Park
description: Public park in Kunjaban area of Agartala featuring miniature replicas of major Tripura heritage sites, tribal huts, gardens and a walking track. Inaugurated in 2012 to showcase the state's cultural and natural heritage.
facts: Inaugurated November 2012
Contains miniature models of Unakoti, Neermahal, Tripura Sundari and other sites
Spread over about 4-12 hectares with walking track
Located near Kunjaban / northern Agartala

name: Agartala
description: Capital city of Tripura and headquarters of West Tripura district. Gateway with airport and railway connections; hosts major royal palaces, temples, museums and serves as base for exploring the state.
facts: Capital and largest city of Tripura
HQ of West Tripura district
Connected by air (IXA), rail and road
Main base for visiting palaces and nearby attractions
